recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-14719 unless PA/Gender Harmony makes a new decision to restore direct base-spec guidance for clinical gender or birth-sex exchange rather than relying on the current Patient section, Extension Pack content, and Gender Harmony IG.
issue_request: FHIR-14719 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification STU3 Patient issue asking for better patient gender representation guidance: remove the old Meaningful Use-specific birth-sex wording, avoid a US Core link, add and reference a Clinical Gender Observation example, and include the Gender Identity standard extension from FHIR-13843.
initial_application: The issue family was applied in 2018. Commit 7fa7a34f97 (#14482) rewrote Patient Gender and Sex and removed the old Meaningful Use birth-sex sentence. Commit f71751e893, explicitly marked part of GF#14719, created the clinical-gender Observation example. Commit b7d0f473c3 explicitly named 14719 and 14754, linked the example from the Patient guidance, and corrected the US-specific birth-sex wording.
additional_context: Later Patient Administration and Gender Harmony decisions intentionally changed the model. FHIR-29673 refreshed Patient sex/gender guidance around Gender Identity, SPCU, clinical observations, RSG, Legal Sex, and Sex assigned at Birth. FHIR-39203 moved sex/gender exchange recommendations out of FHIR base and into the Gender Harmony IG. Related Patient sex/gender issues FHIR-14754, FHIR-14755, FHIR-14756, FHIR-29673, and FHIR-38861 already have combined-branch audits.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source no longer contains the old gender-section Meaningful Use birth-sex sentence; the Patient Gender and Sex section reflects later approved guidance; the Clinical Gender Observation example still exists and is listed; and Gender Identity is represented through current Patient links and Extension Pack definitions. Reintroducing the old direct Patient-page clinical gender or birth-sex exchange wording would partially reverse later Gender Harmony decisions.
